description: Verify that DUT does NOT auto-configure an IPv4 Link-Local address while a routable DHCP lease is available (RFC 3927 §1.9 SHOULD NOT)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 3927 §1.9 says a host SHOULD NOT configure a Link-Local address (169.254/16) while it has a routable IP from a higher-priority source such as DHCP. This case checks that DUT successfully completes a DHCPv4 lease and then stays on the routable address — it must not start the Link-Local probe machine on the side.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester (DHCP server emul) ⇄ DUT: full DHCPv4 4-way exchange
   • DUT emits DISCOVER → tester replies OFFER on Listening_for_request entry
   • DUT emits REQUEST → tester replies ACK on Listening_for_no_arp_probe entry
   • Lease time = 15 s (ParamListenTime × 3, per TC8 §3 default 5 s)

2. Observation (Listening_for_no_arp_probe window):
   • DUT must NOT emit any ARP Probe targeting a 169.254/16 address

[Pass condition]
DISCOVER → OFFER → REQUEST → ACK observed AND no Link-Local ARP Probe within the listen window.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_discover — DUT did not emit DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
• Fail_no_request — DUT did not emit DHCPREQUEST after receiving the OFFER
• Fail_dut_emitted_ll_probe — DUT emitted a Link-Local ARP Probe even though it had a routable lease

verdicts.Pass: DUT honoured the DHCP lease and stayed off Link-Local — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: DUT did not emit DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
verdicts.Fail_no_request: DUT did not emit DHCPREQUEST after the OFFER
verdicts.Fail_dut_emitted_ll_probe: DUT emitted a Link-Local ARP Probe despite having a routable DHCP lease
